correctness.rationale: The support identifies onset. For s>0, s log(C sqrt(s)) is a quadratic in s with coefficients -B, ell_j, -A_j; three distinct known-onset sampling times recover them. Upstream, the positive distance ratio sqrt(A_1/A_0) determines location and then D; the spatial amplitude slope gives v/D and the remaining coefficients give k and M. The one-station scaling preserves all three invariants and stays admissible. Without the side prior, scaling the two absolute distances by q=L/(2p+L) gives an interior source, D'=q²D and v'=q²v. The prescribed k' and M' match B and both amplitudes, with k'>=0 and v'>0. The equal-ratio degenerate case has only a midpoint source, not an extra same-side solution. Three spatial samples of the exact squared-distance quadratic determine its leading and linear coefficients and hence D and location. Independently substituting the same-mass example gives A_0=1/4, A_1=1, B=1+9(log 3)²/16, common spatial amplitude slope and common ell_0; q exp(v(eta-xi)/(2D))=1. Thus it is an all-time alias in the physical domain, not a numerical match.
residual_risks: No claim for sensor/source coincidences, unobserved onset in the finite-sampling assertion, or noise. The recorded numerical diagnostics are auxiliary and were not rerun.

originality.rationale: The absolute-distance obstruction and three-station quadratic interpolation substantially overlap earlier zero-drift diffusion geometry and are not credited as independent discoveries. In fact the factor exp((v/D)x/2-Bs) can be peeled off, leaving pure diffusion with effective mass M exp(-(v/D)xi/2). The peeled model clarifies what is inherited and why effective-mass calibration is different from physical-mass calibration. The distinct claim supported by the inspected evidence is the side-prior inverse with all transport parameters unknown, including the cross-side transformation satisfying the physical inequalities and colliding at exactly the same prescribed physical mass for positive drift.
residual_risks: Several relevant river inverse papers were not readable, including the ScienceDirect hit PII S0269749121010794. A stronger unknown-coefficient theorem elsewhere remains possible.
No claim to historical uniqueness of Gaussian spatial interpolation, the gauge transform, or the three-sensor principle alone.

value.rationale: The branch classification answers a concrete monitoring-design question in a natural ideal tracer model: a location prior substitutes for a third station, while exact mass calibration cannot always do so. The positive-drift same-mass witness is decisive even when entire traces are available; it separates structural ambiguity from noise and avoidable fitting errors.
residual_risks: The result does not justify real-river inference, sample conditioning, or operational sensor placement outside the assumed free-line model.
